info.title: npm Publication Monitor API
info.summary: Read the journal, stage results, alerts and statistics of the npm publication monitor; record analyst verdicts.
info.description:
The monitor reads the npm registry change feed, scores every publication on the metadata layer in two stages and stores an evidence snapshot per enriched event.
This API is what the single-page dashboard uses. All read endpoints are public within the deployment; the two write operations (`PUT` and `DELETE /events/{seq}/finding`) require the analyst bearer token.

### Real-time feed (WebSocket)
Connect to `ws(s)://<host>/npm/api/v1/ws`. The server pushes JSON messages, one for each change:
- `{"type":"event","event":Event}` — a new journal event (stage results are `null` and arrive later);
- `{"type":"stage1","seq":…,"stage1":Stage1Summary}` — stage 1 found at least one feature on the event (an event without a feature gets no message);
- `{"type":"stage2","seq":…,"stage2":Stage2Summary}` — stage 2 finished the event (alerts have `stage2.alert = true`);
- `{"type":"status","status":Status}` — pipeline status, every 10 s;
- `{"type":"hello","last_seq":…}` — first message after connect, the newest seq the server has sent to its clients, so the client can backfill with `GET /events?after=`.
Clients send nothing; the connection is read-only. Reconnect with back-off; after a reconnect the client reads what it missed over REST (`GET /events?after=`).

### Conventions
- **Versioning:** the major version is in the path (`/api/v1`); additions are backward compatible, a breaking change gets a new path. See `documentation/api/reference/versioning.md`.
- **Errors:** every error is `{"error": "<message>"}` with a 4xx or 5xx status; the message names the parameter that was rejected.
- **Pagination:** lists of events use a cursor (`before`, `after`, `limit`) and return `next_before`.
- **Time:** ISO 8601 in UTC. **Names:** `snake_case` fields, plural resource names.

Guides and tutorials: `documentation/api/` in the repository.

get.description: Positions and lag of the collector and both stages, the size of the enrichment queue, the date of the watchlist snapshot and the start of the journal. The dashboard polls it and also receives it over the WebSocket.
Returns 200 when the collector polled within the last 5 minutes and stage 1 is less than 5 000 events behind; otherwise 503 with the reasons. Suitable for an uptime check that alerts on failure.
Cursor-paginated journal. Filters narrow the set before pagination. Use `after` with the `last_seq` from the WebSocket `hello` message to backfill a live feed.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Return events with seq strictly below this value (cursor pagination, newest first).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return events with seq strictly above this value (oldest first). Mutually exclusive with `before`.

parameters.name: flagged
parameters.description: Only events with at least one stage-1 feature

parameters.name: feature
parameters.description: Only events where this feature id fired (stage 1 or stage 2)

post.summary: Alerts on the packages of one consumer
post.description: Takes a list of package names, for example the names of a lock file, and returns the alerts on these packages for the last days with the count per day. The request reads only; it is a POST because the list does not fit a URL. The list is not stored.

example.error: packages must be a non-empty array of package names

get.description: The event, both stage results in full (including the stage-2 evidence snapshot and per-source answers), the analyst finding and the other journal events of the same package.

put.summary: Record or change the analyst verdict
put.description: Stores one verdict per event. The call is idempotent: the same body gives the same stored verdict, a different body replaces it. Every change is kept in an audit table of the database.

reference.description: Advisory, issue or write-up that confirms the finding

example.note: nightly build from the project CI

example.error: verdict must be one of confirmed, false_positive, undecided

delete.description: Deletes the verdict of the event; the audit table keeps the removed value. Deleting a verdict that does not exist also answers 204.

get.description: Every stored verdict, newest first; `verdict` narrows the list to one value.

Error.description: Every error answer. The message names the rejected parameter; it is meant for a developer, not for an end user.

Feature.description: One fired feature with the value that fired it, the threshold and the weight it adds to the score.

Finding.description: Manual verdict of an analyst on an event — the ground truth used by the evaluation.

reference.description: Advisory, issue or write-up that confirms the finding

Event.description: A journal event with the stage results attached when they exist.

observed_after.description: Lower bound of the moment the event appeared in the feed; null for backfilled history.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` to fetch the next (older) page; null when exhausted.

items.description: Alerts of the period, newest first, at most 500
